text:
Maria (runtime): heads-up — after last week's deploy I started seeing a weird latency jitter tail on a subset of tenants, not raw p99 jumps but sporadic 40–120ms spikes for streaming responses.
Devon: ugh, saw that too in dashboard. looks correlated with handoff events?
Maria (runtime): yes. spikes line up with batch handoffs where a hot tenant gets moved between lanes. pattern: steady low latency, then ~10–30s window of jitter, then back to baseline.
Lee: can you paste an example trace?
Maria (runtime): pasted a condensed sample log below:
```
# simplified runtime trace
[11:03:21] serve: request A enter lane-3
[11:03:21] serve: request B (hot-tenant) preempt -> lane-1
[11:03:22] batch-cut: lane-1 flush (size 32) -> kernel switch
[11:03:22] kvcache: attach/detach events -> small stall 85ms
[11:03:25] requests resume
```
Sasha: that kernel switch + kvcache attach/detach smell like cold path thrash. when tenants move we rebind KV pages which blocks the fastpath.
Devon: agree. two levers: avoid moving hot tenants too often, or make the handoff nonblocking (incremental attach?).
Lee: metric-wise, we could emit a "handoff_jitter" signal: sample per-tenant token-latency delta before/after handoff and tag traces. lightweight sampling every N handoffs.
Maria (runtime): prototyping sampling now. config idea:
```
hand_off_sampling:
  sample_rate: 0.1 # sample 1 in 10 handoffs
  windows: [5s, 30s] # pre/post windows to compute delta
  emit: traces + histogram
```
Devon: nice. also we should classify handoffs: graceful (drain + poke) vs forceful (immediate move). impacts strategy.
Sasha: for graceful we can queue a tiny microbatch to keep kv handles alive during the move. basically keep an anchor on the old lane until the new lane warmed KV. cheap ping tokens.
Lee: how cheap? does that affect SLOs for others? we need a fairness budget. maybe amortize across tenants with low QoS impact.
Maria (runtime): thinking of a "handoff token pool" approach — N tokens reserved per GPU, used to send sub-ms anchor ops that preserve cache residency. token consumption tracked and billed internally to tenant budget.
Devon: can we simulate in the scheduler first? run a replay with injected handoffs + token anchors and measure tail.
Sasha: yes. I can add a simulator mode flag: --simulate-anchor=true that treats an anchor op as +1 token in batch shaping and models kernel switch cost.
Maria (runtime): if anchors reduce jitter, we need eviction rules: if anchor budget exhausted, fallback to immediate move but emit alert. also add adaptive token refill when jitter grows.
Lee: also consider smoothing window when deciding to move: if a tenant has moving-average latency slope > threshold, delay move until slope flat. basically avoid cutting the line while it's hot.
Devon: two tradeoffs: increased latency for the moved tenant (if we delay) vs jitter risk for everyone if we move now. need policy knobs per SLA tier.
Sasha: proposal: default strategy for free/low-tier = immediate move (no anchors), mid-tier = anchors with low budget, enterprise = reserved lanes / canary handoffs. document in rollout plan.
Maria (runtime): sounds good. next steps: 1) land sampling + handoff_jitter metric (Sasha/Lee), 2) add simulator anchor mode (Sasha), 3) run replay (Devon), 4) PR for token-pool proto + policy knobs (Maria).
Devon: I'll prep a replay job and share results in #eng-runtime-playback.
Lee: I'll sketch PromQL for the handoff_jitter metric and a dashboard delta panel.
Sasha: starting sampler PR today, will ping when ready for review.
infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: canary rollout 10% -> 25% at 12:00 UTC (FYI).
Maria (runtime): ok keep an eye on the canary and watch handoff_jitter after each step. ping me if you see a >30ms median delta. :eyes:
Devon: ping noted. thanks all.
